candidateConcepts.rationale: Core life-safety path of travel used to move occupants from the workplace to a safe discharge during an emergency.
The number of exit routes must be adequate for building size, occupancy, arrangement, and safe evacuation.
Exit-route capacity must support the maximum permitted occupant load and may not decrease toward discharge.
Occupant load is a key input to exit-route quantity, capacity, and width decisions.
Exit discharge connects the protected route to the outside, public way, refuge area, or open space with outside access.
Protected exits require separation from other workplace areas by specified fire-resistant construction.
Door swing direction becomes a life-safety design requirement for rooms with more than 50 occupants or high-hazard contents.
Exit routes must remain free and unobstructed so emergency travel is not compromised.
Walking-working surfaces must support the maximum intended load, directly addressing the blueprint's floor-loading example.
